key_insight: Organic photovoltaic performance depends primarily on CT–CS energy alignment, while fast triplet recycling helps preserve the balance between charge generation and voltage loss.
engineering_relevance: The model suggests targeting LE–CT offsets of 0.15–0.20 eV, weakly exothermic CT–CS offsets of 0.05–0.075 eV, and CT–T offsets no greater than about 0.1 eV.
method: Couple singlet and triplet exciton kinetics with drift–diffusion charge transport.
Solve state populations and reversible transitions self-consistently.
Evaluate transient and steady-state responses across energy offsets and triplet-transfer rates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproduction of triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends, but provides no quantitative validation metrics.
watch_item: This is a physics-based device model, not an AI method; the proposed design windows require broader experimental validation.
paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
